tagline: The first coast-to-coast road, all the way across Nebraska.
intro: US 30 comes in from Wyoming to Kimball, a town that calls itself the high point of Nebraska although the actual summit, Panorama Point, is some 33 miles off. The road runs east through Sidney and Ogallala to North Platte, then on through Gothenburg, Kearney, Grand Island and Columbus to Blair, near the Missouri.

This was the Lincoln Highway, dedicated in 1913 to run from Times Square to San Francisco, and its midpoint falls at Kearney. The emigrant trails, the Pony Express and the transcontinental railroad all came along the Platte before it. In Gothenburg a Pony Express station, moved in off a ranch in 1931, stands in a town park.

moments.title: Ogallala
moments.text: The railhead where the Texas cattle drives ended, and where the cowboys earned the place the name The Town Too Tough for Texas.

moments.title: North Platte
moments.text: From Christmas Day 1941 until 1946 Nebraska women met the troop trains at the Union Pacific depot, serving almost seven million soldiers in stops of ten or fifteen minutes.

moments.title: Columbus
moments.text: Andrew Higgins, born here, designed the Higgins boat, a landing craft used in World War II, and in Pawnee Park a life-size one lets bronze soldiers out onto sand gathered from 58 beaches.
